content.text: The verifier's narrative confirms the handling: compliant, no redline, no comment. The failed deterministic "audit frequency limited" check is an artefact of there being no audit clause at all, not a drafting defect. I'll resubmit with that point made explicit.

input.quote: Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4) and will be entitled to contest any charge
input.rationale: No audit, inspection, records-examination or usage-verification right runs against Mortgage Logic.com anywhere in the Agreement. Sections 2-4 (license/services), 5-6 (compensation), 7 (spamming), 8 (Client covenants) and 10 (confidentiality) were reviewed in full, and searches for "audit", "inspect", "records", "books", "examine", "verif", "monitor" and "premises" returned no hits. The verification-type mechanics that do exist run in our favour: §6 entitles us to supporting documentation for charges and to contest them, and §3(e) gives us real-time access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files. The nearest TrueLink-side rights are §8(f) (TrueLink may implement technical mechanisms to prevent spamming) and §9 (we give reasonable access so TrueLink can make Y2K repairs and upgrades at its sole cost) - both are narrow, self-funded Vendor rights, not audits of our usage, and neither creates frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access exposure. Silence is better for us than the AUDIT preferred position, so no redline is warranted: inserting frequency/notice/cost parameters would create an audit right TrueLink does not currently have. The deterministic "audit frequency limited" check fails only because there is no audit clause to carry a frequency limit, not because of defective drafting, so it reflects no unaddressed risk. If TrueLink later seeks a usage-audit right, we would require the preferred terms (once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, TrueLink's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no direct access to our systems).
